title: `elementDataSourceViewNotFoundMessage` states "This object has no saved views." on a read that never happened — the second consumer of the objectui#8151 swallow
body:
⛔ **Ungraded and unrouted** — `domain:*`, priority and type are triage's. Filed unassigned, out of scope, from the objectui#8151 round. ⛔ Not filed as a duplicate of objectui#8151: that card's delivery is the adapter-side discrimination plus the toast, and this sentence survives it intact.

## The behaviour

Measured on `origin/main` `b686ebf7d`.

`packages/core/src/data-scope/element-data-source.ts`, `elementDataSourceViewNotFoundMessage`, the `knownViews.length` ternary:

```js
const known = knownViews.length
  ? `Known views: ${[...knownViews].sort().join(', ')}.`
  : 'This object has no saved views.';
```

`knownViews` is filled by `fetchSavedViews` in `packages/react/src/hooks/useElementDataSource.ts`, whose overlay leg is:

```js
const overlay = canReadOverlay
  ? dataSource.listViews(object).then((rows) => rows, () => undefined)
  : Promise.resolve(undefined);
```

That leg maps a REJECTION to `undefined` — a deliberate discrimination, and the right one. But `ObjectStackAdapter.listViews` **never rejects**: it degrades every failure to `[]` (that is the shipped, deliberate contract, and objectui#8151 explicitly keeps it). So a refused or broken `view` read arrives here as an EMPTY ARRAY on the resolved path, `collectSavedViews` contributes nothing, `knownViews.length` is `0`, and the renderer states as fact:

> `dataSource.view "X" was not found on object "Y". This object has no saved views.`

Both halves of that sentence are unsupported by what actually happened. Nobody found out whether the object has saved views.

The sentence is pinned, so it is a live surface and not dead code: `packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/ListView.elementDataSource.test.tsx:283` asserts the rendered panel contains `no saved views`, and `packages/core/src/data-scope/__tests__/element-data-source.test.ts` has the unit pin beside it.

## Why objectui#8151 does not close this

objectui#8151 adds the discrimination at the adapter and announces it on `onMetadataReadWarning`, which `app-shell`'s `AdapterProvider` renders as a toast. That is a real improvement and this card is not a complaint about it. It is not enough here for two measured reasons:

1. **The toast is beside the lie, not instead of it.** Under `AdapterProvider` a user now gets a warning toast AND a config-error panel that still says the object has no saved views. A transient toast does not retract a sentence sitting on screen.
2. **This consumer is not in `app-shell`.** `useElementDataSource` lives in `@object-ui/react` and this message is rendered by `@object-ui/plugin-list`'s `ConfigError`. A host that composes those packages without `AdapterProvider` subscribes to nothing at all and sees only the sentence.

## Why this is its own card and was not folded in

objectui#8151's dispatch scoped it to `listViews`'s catch arm and the warning channel, and said in as many words ⛔ 不要顺手改 the empty-state copy — measure it, name a successor, do not widen the surface. This is that successor. The repair also belongs to a different package pair (`@object-ui/core` + `@object-ui/react`) than the one that card touches, and it has a design question objectui#8151 has no standing to answer:

- `fetchSavedViews` already distinguishes "could not read" from "read, found none" — for the REJECTION shape. The adapter's contract is that it never rejects, so the distinction has no way to arrive. Does the fix teach that hook to consult `onMetadataReadWarning`, does `composeElementDataSource` take a third state, or does the sentence simply stop making the claim (`Known views could not be read.`)? That is a contract decision, not a copy edit.

## Re-check

```sh
git -C objectui grep -n "no saved views" origin/main -- packages/core packages/react packages/plugin-list
```

Three hits on `origin/main` `b686ebf7d`: the declaration in `element-data-source.ts`, and the two pins.

## Related

**objectui#8151** (the adapter-side discrimination this was found from) · **objectui#7741** (the sibling one method over) · **objectui#7143** (`ListView` rendering a load FAILURE through `DataEmptyState`, closed — same family of confusion, a different surface) · **#13906** decision 1 option A (*a thing that could not be READ is not a thing that is ABSENT*, the governing discrimination).
